description: Figure 2 is a conceptual diagram illustrating five distinct layer grouping patterns for model design, with the horizontal axis representing four sequential groups (G₁ through G₄) and the vertical axis representing the number of layers assigned to each group. The figure visually depicts five patterns: (i) Increasing, where the number of layers rises progressively from G₁ to G₄; (ii) Uniform, where each group contains an equal number of layers; (iii) Decreasing, where the number of layers declines from G₁ to G₄; (iv) Spindle, where the middle groups (G₂ and G₃) have more layers than the end groups (G₁ and G₄); and (v) Bottleneck, where the middle groups have fewer layers than the end groups. Each pattern is represented by a distinct shape or trend line connecting the layer counts across the four groups, providing a visual comparison of how layers can be distributed among model segments.
